title: Design: Replace the nightly batch with a Kafka event stream

defects.quote: Kafka was originally built at Twitter
defects.correction: Apache Kafka was originally developed at LinkedIn.
defects.note: [multi-part] The second fact in the sentence (open-sourced in 2011) is true; only the company is wrong.

defects.quote: Kafka guarantees that messages are delivered in order across all partitions of a topic
defects.correction: Kafka guarantees ordering only within a single partition, not across the partitions of a topic.
defects.note: [secondary-source] Top results are likely blog posts and Q&A threads; the primary source is the Apache Kafka documentation.

defects.quote: Kafka keeps messages for 30 days by default
defects.correction: Kafka's default log retention is 7 days (log.retention.hours=168).
defects.note: [secondary-source] The primary source is the broker configuration reference in the Apache Kafka documentation.

defects.quote: Streaming pipelines cost 50% less to run than batch jobs at our volume.
Batch is legacy technology and streaming is the industry standard, so we should migrate every pipeline.
defects.known_rebuttal: The requirement is data freshness, not fashion. Only pipelines whose consumers need low latency benefit from streaming; reports that are read once a day gain nothing from second-level freshness. Streaming adds standing costs that batch does not have: a cluster to operate and be on call for, schema evolution, late and out-of-order data, duplicate handling and harder backfills. Batch jobs are simpler to rerun and audit, so the migration should be decided per pipeline, by need.

defects.quote: Their is no plan yet for who will be on call for the cluster.
defects.note: Copy editor (grammar) and structure reviewer (no operational ownership or on-call plan) both flag this sentence; they should be merged into one finding.
[multi-part] The true half of the sentence that also carries d1; a rebuttal disputing this fact must be discarded.

defects.quote: Kafka guarantees that messages are delivered in order across all partitions of a topic, so the warehouse loader do not need to handle out-of-order updates.
defects.note: 'do' should be 'does', but the sentence carries a wrong fact, so the fact finding wins.
